about: Phenom is an Ambler, Pennsylvania HR technology company, offering an AI-driven talent experience platform with career sites, recruiting automation, employee development and talent marketing. Customers are large employers across industries, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2010, it raised about $161 million. B2B HR software brand with limited consumer awareness. It competes with other talent acquisition and recruiting platforms and sells to human resources and recruiting departments of large employers, so awareness is limited to HR technology buyers.

Scality is a San Francisco, with French roots, software-defined object storage company whose RING and ARTESCA products store and manage very large volumes of unstructured data for cloud, telecoms, media and healthcare customers. Customers are large enterprises, paying licences and subscriptions. Founded in 2009, it raised about $172 million. B2B storage brand with no consumer awareness. It competes with large storage vendors, and its software is deployed in service provider and enterprise data centres, so its name is known to infrastructure buyers but not consumers.

wiki.title: Scality
wiki.text: Scality is a global technology provider of software-defined storage (SDS) solutions, specializing in distributed file and object storage with cloud data management. Scality maintains offices in Paris (France), London (UK), San Francisco and Washington DC (USA), and Tokyo (Japan) and has employees in 14 countries.

about: Weave is a Lehi, Utah software company providing patient communication, scheduling, payments and AI phone tools for small healthcare practices such as dentists and optometrists. Customers are small medical offices, paying monthly subscriptions. Founded in 2008, it listed on the NYSE (WEAV) in 2021. Crunchbase shows about $172 million of pre-IPO funding. B2B healthcare software brand with little consumer awareness.

Lansweeper is a Merelbeke, Belgium IT asset discovery and inventory software company that scans networks to give IT and security teams a complete view of hardware, software and cyber risks. Customers are companies of all sizes, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2004, it raised about EUR 130 million in a 2021 round led by Insight Partners. B2B software brand with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Lansweeper
wiki.text: Lansweeper is an IT discovery & inventory platform which delivers insights into the status of users, devices, and software within IT environments. This platform inventories connected IT devices, enabling organizations to centrally manage their IT infrastructure. Lansweeper's automated processes identify and compile a list of connected devices, including computers, routers, servers, and printers. It furnishes device-specific information covering installed software, applied updates & patches, and user details.

about: Clarivate is an information services company, headquartered in London and Philadelphia and incorporated in Jersey, that provides research and IP data to universities, governments and companies. Its brands include Web of Science, Journal Citation Reports, Derwent, CompuMark trademark services, Cortellis life-sciences data and, after 2021, ProQuest. It was spun out of Thomson Reuters in 2016 and listed on the NYSE as CLVT through a 2019 SPAC merger. Revenue is around 2.5 billion dollars, with roughly 11,000 staff. B2B, well known in academia but not to consumers.

wiki.title: Clarivate
wiki.text: Clarivate Plc (Clarivate) is a British-American publicly traded analytics company operating a collection of subscription-based services in the areas of bibliometrics and scientometrics, business and market intelligence, and competitive profiling for pharmacy and biotech, patents, regulatory compliance, trademark protection, and domain and brand protection. Clarivate calculates the impact factor of scientific journals using data from its family of Web of Science products, including services and applications such as Publons, EndNote, and EndNote Click. Clarivate's other product families are Cortellis, Decision Resources Group (DRG), CPA Global,

about: Semantix is a Sao Paulo data and artificial intelligence software company that offers a data platform, analytics and AI tools to Latin American enterprises, helping banks, retailers and telecoms organise and exploit data. Customers pay software and service fees. It listed on Nasdaq as STIX in 2022 through a merger with a special-purpose acquisition company, Alpha Capital. It is a small-to-mid-size company by revenue, with offices in Brazil and other Latin American countries. B2B, with little consumer brand awareness.

Liquidnet was a US institutional trading network based in New York, known for dark pool block trading that lets asset managers trade large share blocks anonymously without moving the market. It also provided analytics, research and fixed income execution services. TP ICAP acquired it in late 2021 for about 575 million dollars, and it now operates inside TP ICAP. Customers were asset managers and brokers. B2B financial brand with no consumer awareness.
flags: last funding 2005: check it is still independent and operating

wiki.title: Liquidnet
wiki.text: Liquidnet is a global institutional trading and investment network that connects asset managers with liquidity. Founded in 2001, the company provides electronic services for more than 1,000 asset management firms across 46 markets.

about: Dashlane is a password manager and credential security company, founded in Paris and now headquartered in New York. It sells apps and browser extensions that store and autofill passwords, flag breaches and offer a VPN, to individual consumers and businesses on subscription plans. It has millions of users and raised about 211 million dollars. Moderate consumer brand awareness among tech users, with strong online marketing.

wiki.title: Dashlane
wiki.text: Dashlane is a subscription-based password manager and digital wallet application available on macOS, Windows, iOS and Android, founded in Paris. Dashlane uses a subscription business model option.

about: Encora is a US software engineering and digital technology services firm based in Santa Clara, California, with delivery centres in Latin America, India and Eastern Europe. It provides outsourced product development, cloud, data and AI engineering for software companies and enterprises. It is private equity backed by Advent International and Warburg Pincus, grew through acquisitions, and has about 200 million dollars of reported funding. B2B services brand with no consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Encora accelerates business outcomes for clients through...

about: Appier is an artificial intelligence software company listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, founded in Taiwan and operating across Asia-Pacific. It offers AI-powered marketing, advertising and customer data tools that help brands acquire, engage and retain customers, with customers in e-commerce, retail, finance and travel. Funding of about 164 million dollars was raised before its 2021 IPO. B2B marketing technology brand with strong awareness among Asian marketers.

wiki.title: Kevin Appier
wiki.text: Robert Kevin Appier is an American former professional baseball pitcher who played 16 seasons in Major League Baseball (MLB), primarily for the Kansas City Royals.

wiki.title: Forcepoint
wiki.text: Forcepoint is an American multinational corporation software company headquartered in Austin, Texas, that develops computer security software and data protection, cloud access security broker, firewall and cross-domain solutions.

about: Dixa is a Danish customer service software company headquartered in Copenhagen. Its cloud platform unifies calls, chat, email and messaging and uses AI to route and automate conversations for customer service teams. Customers are mid-size and large consumer-facing companies in Europe and North America, paying subscription fees. Founded in 2015 from a merger of Dixa and Elmer, it raised about $158 million, including a 2021 round. It is a B2B software brand with limited consumer awareness but strong presence at Nordic tech events.

wiki.title: Dixa
wiki.text: Dixa is a genus of midges, belonging to the family Dixidae.

about: Sprout Social sells cloud software that helps companies manage social media: publishing and scheduling, a unified inbox, listening and analytics, employee advocacy, and influencer marketing tools. Customers are marketers, agencies and customer-care teams at businesses of all sizes, which pay recurring subscriptions, with roughly 30,000 paying customers and revenue above 400 million dollars. Founded in 2010 in Chicago and listed on Nasdaq (SPT) since 2019. It has acquired Simply Measured, Tagger and NewsWhip. B2B software brand with moderate awareness among marketers but little with the general public. A natural fit for brand-activation and content storytelling deals around event sponsorship.

wiki.title: Sprout Social
wiki.text: Sprout Social, Inc. is a technology company that runs a social media management platform. A public company headquartered in Chicago, it was founded in 2010 by Justyn Howard, Aaron Rankin, Gil Lara, and Peter Soung.

about: PowerFleet is a US provider of Internet of Things (IoT) solutions for asset management: devices and software that track and manage vehicles, trailers, forklifts, containers and industrial equipment. Its products include Unity, Pointer and Fleet Complete lines, serving logistics, retail, transport and manufacturing customers on subscription plans and with RFID hardware. Based in New Jersey, with operations in Israel and Brazil, and listed on Nasdaq (PWFL). Acquired Fleet Complete in 2024. B2B brand with limited public awareness.

wiki.title: Powerfleet
wiki.text: Powerfleet, Inc. is an American company headquartered in Woodcliff Lake, New Jersey, that operates as a global provider of IoT and M2M solutions for securing, controlling, and tracking high-value enterprise assets. The company is a provider in the international telematics industry, providing fleet management, asset tracking, freight visibility, and driver behavior monitoring for industrial trucks, vehicle fleets, and shipping containers.

about: Calix is a San Jose, California company, listed on the NYSE (CALX), that supplies cloud software, platforms and systems to broadband service providers, such as rural and regional telecoms, cable and fibre operators. Its Calix Cloud, Revenue EDGE and Intelligent Access EDGE platforms, together with Smart Home and Business services and AXOS network software, help providers deliver and manage broadband for homes and businesses. Founded in 1999, it has about 1,800 employees, annual revenue of around 800 million dollars, and customers across North America. B2B brand strong among broadband operators, with no consumer name recognition.
flags: listed (IPO status: public); last funding 2009: check it is still independent and operating

about: Network performance monitoring and cybersecurity company. It sells packet-flow visibility, service assurance and DDoS protection through its Arbor Networks business, plus Omnis and nGeniusONE products, to telecom carriers, large enterprises and governments. It grew by acquiring Danaher's communications business, including Tektronix Communications, Arbor and Fluke Networks, in 2015. Revenue is roughly 800 to 900 million dollars. Listed on Nasdaq as NTCT. B2B infrastructure software with low consumer awareness.
flags: listed (IPO status: public); last funding 1999: check it is still independent and operating

about: Internet infrastructure company that operates the authoritative registry for the .com and .net domain names and runs two of the world's thirteen root name servers. Revenue, roughly 1.5 billion dollars a year, comes from per-domain registry fees paid via registrars, with very high operating margins. Berkshire Hathaway is a large shareholder. Listed on Nasdaq as VRSN. B2B critical infrastructure; the .com brand is globally recognised, but VeriSign itself has little consumer profile.
flags: listed (IPO status: public); last funding 1996: check it is still independent and operating

wiki.title: Verisign
wiki.text: Verisign, Inc. is an American company based in Reston, Virginia, that operates a diverse array of network infrastructure, including two of the Internet's thirteen root nameservers, the authoritative registry for the .com, .net, .web and .name generic top-level domains and the .cc country-code top-level domains, and the back-end systems for the .jobs and .edu sponsored top-level domains.

about: Identity security software company selling cloud platforms to govern who has access to applications, data and cloud resources, including identity governance, access management and AI-driven risk tools. Customers are large enterprises and governments, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2005 and based in Austin, it IPO'd on the NYSE in 2017, was taken private by Thoma Bravo in 2022, then relisted on Nasdaq in 2025 as SAIL. B2B security brand, known to CIOs more than consumers.
flags: listed (IPO status: public); last funding 2014: check it is still independent and operating

about: Cybersecurity company offering managed detection and response and extended detection services through its Taegis XDR platform, plus incident response and threat intelligence. Customers are mid-sized and large enterprises and public bodies worldwide; revenue is mostly subscriptions, around $350m a year before acquisition. Founded in 1999 and spun out of Dell, which held the majority stake. Listed on Nasdaq (SCWX) until Sophos bought it in a deal announced in late 2024 and completed in early 2025. B2B brand known to security buyers only.

wiki.title: Secureworks
wiki.text: Secureworks Inc. was an American cybersecurity company. The company had approximately 4,000 customers in more than 50 countries, ranging from Fortune 100 companies to mid-sized businesses in a variety of industries.

about: AST SpaceMobile is a Midland, Texas company building a space-based cellular broadband network of large low-earth-orbit satellites that connect directly to ordinary smartphones. Partners include AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone and Rakuten, and it has launched its BlueBird satellites. It earns revenue from wholesale service with mobile operators and government deals. Listed on Nasdaq (ASTS) after a 2021 SPAC merger. Pre-commercial technology company, with growing investor awareness but no consumer brand.

wiki.title: AST SpaceMobile
wiki.text: AST SpaceMobile, Inc. is a publicly traded satellite designer and manufacturer based in Midland, Texas, United States. The company is building the SpaceMobile satellite constellation, a space-based cellular broadband network designed to connect directly to standard, unmodified smartphones. The network is intended to deliver 4G and 5G broadband coverage globally, particularly in remote and underserved regions.

about: SBA Communications is a Boca Raton, Florida owner and operator of wireless towers, with about 40,000 sites across the US and Latin America leased to carriers such as AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile. It earns recurring lease revenue, about $2.7bn per year, and is organised as a REIT. Listed on Nasdaq (SBAC). B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand profile.

wiki.title: SBA Communications
wiki.text: SBA Communications Corporation is a real estate investment trust which owns and operates wireless infrastructure in the United States, Canada, Central America, South America, and South Africa. It was founded in 1989 as Steven Bernstein and Associates by Steven Bernstein.

about: Zayo is a Denver-based fibre network and bandwidth provider operating long-haul and metro fibre across North America and Europe, selling dark fibre, wavelengths and Ethernet to carriers, hyperscalers and enterprises. It was taken private in 2020 by Digital Colony and EQT for about $14bn and agreed to acquire Crown Castle's fibre business in 2025. Private. B2B network provider, without consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Zayo Group
wiki.text: Zayo Group, Inc. is a digital infrastructure company providing fiber-optic networks, high-capacity connectivity, and networking solutions to enterprises, hyperscalers, cloud and content providers, data centers, and telecommunications carriers worldwide.

about: Cogeco Inc is a Montreal communications holding company that owns Cogeco Communications, which provides cable, internet, TV and phone services to homes and businesses in Quebec and Ontario under Cogeco Connexion and in the US under Breezeline. Customers are residential and business subscribers. Revenue about C$3 billion. Listed on the TSX (CGO). Strong regional consumer brand in Quebec and Ontario, with local sponsorships.

wiki.title: Cogeco
wiki.what: Canadian telecommunications and media company headquartered in Montreal, Quebec
wiki.text: Cogeco Inc. is a Canadian telecommunications and media company. Its corporate offices are located at 1 Place Ville-Marie in Montreal, Quebec. The company is structured into three strategic business units (SBU); Cogeco Connexion, Breezeline, and Cogeco Media. The company provides a range of telecommunication products and services including cable television, radio and television broadcasting, telephony, and Internet services in Ontario and Quebec in Canada, and in thirteen states along the east coast of the United States.

about: Xplore, formerly Xplornet, is a Canadian rural broadband provider offering fibre, fixed wireless and satellite internet, plus 5G fixed wireless, to homes and businesses in rural and underserved areas. Headquartered in Markham, Ontario, serving several hundred thousand subscribers. Owned by private investors including Stonepeak Partners. Crunchbase shows about $1.28 billion in funding. Known as a regional consumer brand in rural Canada.

FiberLight is a US provider of high-capacity fibre-optic network infrastructure, serving carriers, enterprises, government, data centres and wireless providers across several states, with major metro networks in Texas, Georgia, Virginia, Washington DC and the Pacific Northwest. Headquartered in Plano, Texas, it is privately held, funded by infrastructure investors, with funding shown at about 922 million dollars. Revenue is mainly leased dark fibre, wavelengths and backhaul. B2B telecom wholesaler with little consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: FiberLight provides mission critical high performance...

about: Celero Communications is an Irvine, California fabless semiconductor company developing coherent DSP chips and optical connectivity solutions for data center and telecom networks, per Crunchbase, with about $413 million in funding. Customers would be network equipment makers and cloud providers. Private B2B with little public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

KORE Wireless is a US Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity and solutions provider, based in Atlanta, Georgia, offering cellular IoT connectivity management, devices, fleet tracking and analytics to enterprises, healthcare, transportation and industrial customers. It went public in 2021 through a SPAC merger with Cerberus Telecom Acquisition Corp (NYSE: KORE) and has over 18 million connections. B2B with little consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: KORE Wireless
wiki.text: KORE Wireless is a privately-owned company that provides IoT connectivity, managed services, and related solutions. The company supports applications across sectors including healthcare, logistics, fleet, utilities, and industrial automation, with more than 20 million active connections reported worldwide.

about: Bandwidth is a US communications platform-as-a-service company, based in Raleigh, North Carolina, that owns a nationwide IP voice network and sells voice, messaging and 911 APIs to enterprises and software firms, with Microsoft Teams, Zoom and Google as notable users. Founded in 1999, with revenue of about $750 million. Listed on Nasdaq (BAND). B2B, little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Bandwidth Inc.
wiki.text: Bandwidth Inc. is an American communications platform as a service (CPaas) company that provides application programming interfaces (APIs) for voice calling, text messaging, and emergency services. The company operates its own global IP voice network and provides communications infrastructure for businesses and software applications.

about: Ribbon Communications is a Plano, Texas company selling communications software and network equipment, including session border controllers, voice over IP and cloud communications, plus IP optical networking, to telecom carriers and enterprises globally. Formed in 2017 through the merger of Sonus Networks and GENBAND, it is listed on Nasdaq under RBBN, with revenue of around $800 million. B2B technology with no consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Ribbon Communications
wiki.text: Ribbon Communications Inc. is a public company that makes software, IP and optical networking solutions for service providers, enterprises and critical infrastructure sectors. The company was formed in 2017, following the merger of Genband and Sonus Networks and is headquartered in Plano, Texas.

about: Global maker of electrical, electronic and fiber optic connectors, sensors and interconnect systems for the automotive, aerospace, data center, mobile device, industrial and military markets. B2B, selling to OEMs and contract manufacturers with revenue above 15 billion dollars and tens of thousands of employees in many countries. Headquartered in Wallingford, Connecticut; founded 1932. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (APH). Component supplier with minimal consumer awareness, though a large and highly profitable industrial group.

wiki.title: Amphenol
wiki.text: Amphenol Corporation, headquartered in Wallingford, Connecticut, is one of the largest designers, manufacturers and marketers of electrical, electronic and fiber optic connectors and interconnect systems, antennas, sensors and sensor-based products and coaxial, high-speed, fiber optic, and specialty cable.

about: Semiconductor maker producing microcontrollers, analog chips, FPGAs, memory and security devices used in automotive, industrial, aerospace, consumer and data-center applications. B2B, selling through distributors and directly to equipment makers, with revenue around 5 to 8 billion dollars and roughly 20,000 employees. Headquartered in Chandler, Arizona; founded 1989. Listed on Nasdaq (MCHP). The brand is well known to engineers and designers but has little consumer visibility.

wiki.title: Microchip Technology
wiki.text: Microchip Technology Incorporated is an American publicly traded semiconductor corporation that manufactures microcontrollers, microprocessors, integrated circuits, and flash memory.

about: Semiconductor company making power and sensing chips, including silicon carbide power devices and image sensors, for car electrification, ADAS, industrial automation, energy infrastructure and AI data centers. Customers are carmakers and industrial equipment makers, with revenue of roughly 6 to 8 billion dollars. Headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona; formerly ON Semiconductor, with a name change to onsemi in 2021. Listed on Nasdaq (ON). B2B brand with limited public recognition, though it has had motorsport sponsorship links.

wiki.title: Onsemi
wiki.text: ON Semiconductor Corporation is an American semiconductor supplier company, based in Scottsdale, Arizona. Products include power and signal management, logic, discrete, and custom devices for automotive, communications, computing, consumer, industrial, LED lighting, medical, military/aerospace and power applications. onsemi runs a network of manufacturing facilities, sales offices and design centers in North America, Europe, and the Asia Pacific regions. Based on its 2016 revenues of $3.907 billion, onsemi ranked among the worldwide top 20 semiconductor sales leaders, and was ranked No. 483 on the 2022 Fortune 500 based on its 2021 sales.

about: German semiconductor group making power chips, microcontrollers, sensors and security devices for cars, industrial equipment, renewable energy, data centers and payment cards. B2B sales to carmakers and manufacturers, with revenue of about 15 billion euros and over 58,000 employees. Headquartered in Neubiberg near Munich; spun out of Siemens in 1999. Listed in Frankfurt (IFX) and a DAX member. Market leader in automotive and power semiconductors, relatively low consumer visibility though it has sponsored sport, including football clubs and a Formula E team link.

wiki.title: Infineon Technologies
wiki.text: Infineon Technologies AG is a German company which designs and manufactures semiconductor devices. It provides parts for automotive, power and security systems. In 2023, Infineon was Germany's largest chip manufacturer, and had roughly 57,000 employees in 2025.

about: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company is the world's largest contract chipmaker, producing advanced processors for Apple, Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm and others on leading-edge nodes. Revenue is about 90 to 120 billion dollars with margins among the highest in industry. Headquartered in Hsinchu, Taiwan; founded 1987. Listed in Taipei (2330) and New York (TSM), with a market value above 1 trillion dollars. B2B foundry with limited consumer brand awareness and very little traditional sponsorship activity.

Midea Group is one of the world's largest home appliance makers, producing air conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines, kitchenware and robotics (KUKA), plus commercial HVAC and smart building technology. Brands include Midea, Toshiba appliances, Eureka and Clivet. Sells to consumers and businesses worldwide, with revenue near 50 billion dollars and 190,000 employees. Headquartered in Foshan, Guangdong; founded 1968. Listed in Shenzhen (000333) and Hong Kong (0300). Big consumer brand in Asia, with sports sponsorship, including football.

wiki.title: Midea Group
wiki.what: Chinese home appliance manufacturer and air conditioner OEM
wiki.text: Midea Group is a Chinese electrical appliance manufacturer, headquartered in Beijiao town, Shunde District, Foshan, Guangdong and listed on Shenzhen Stock Exchange since 2013. As of 2021, the firm employed approximately 150,000 people in China and overseas with 200 subsidiaries and over 60 overseas branches. It has been listed on the Fortune Global 500 since July 2016. Midea produces lighting, water appliances, floor care, small kitchen appliances, laundry, large cooking appliances, and refrigeration appliances. It is the largest microwave oven manufacturer, and acts as an OEM for many brands. It also has a long history in producing home and

about: Dutch semiconductor maker producing automotive processors, radar, secure identification chips, NFC for payments and passports, and industrial connectivity. Customers are carmakers, phone makers and equipment manufacturers, with revenue of around 12 billion dollars and about 34,000 employees. Headquartered in Eindhoven; spun out of Philips in 2006. Listed on Nasdaq (NXPI). B2B component brand with low consumer awareness but strong ties to automotive, including sports-car partnerships such as the Ferrari Formula 1 connection.

wiki.title: NXP Semiconductors
wiki.text: NXP Semiconductors N.V. is a Dutch multinational semiconductor manufacturing and design company with headquarters in Eindhoven, Netherlands. It is the second-largest European semiconductor design and manufacturing company by market capitalization as of 2024. The company employs approximately 34,000 people in more than 30 countries and it reported revenues of $12.61 billion in 2024. The company's name is an abbreviation of Next eXPerience. NXP customers include Apple, Dell, Ericsson and Samsung.

about: Copeland is a climate technology company making compressors, controls and software for heating, cooling and refrigeration, including the Scroll and Copeland-brand compressors used in HVAC and cold chain systems. Sells to equipment makers and contractors worldwide. Headquartered in St Louis, Missouri (with operations in Sidney, Ohio); formerly Emerson's Climate Technologies, sold in 2023 to Blackstone in a deal that valued the business at about 14 billion dollars, with Emerson retaining a stake. B2B brand with low consumer awareness; the input's consumer electronics tag is inaccurate.

wiki.title: Copeland (company)
wiki.text: Copeland is an American company in the field of heating, cooling, and refrigeration compression technologies and controls solutions.

about: Columbus McKinnon designs and makes material handling equipment, such as hoists, cranes, chain, rigging and lifting products and intelligent motion control, serving industrial, entertainment, infrastructure and construction customers. Revenue near 1 billion dollars. Headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, with historic roots in Amherst, New York; founded 1875. Listed on Nasdaq (CMCO). B2B industrial brand with no consumer visibility, though its hoists are used in stage rigging.

VIAVI Solutions makes network test, measurement and assurance equipment and software for telecom carriers, data centers and cable operators, plus optical security and anti-counterfeiting coatings used on banknotes and in consumer electronics. Customers are network equipment makers, service providers and governments, with revenue near 1 billion dollars. Headquartered in Chandler, Arizona (formerly San Jose); spun out of JDS Uniphase in 2015. Listed on Nasdaq (VIAV). B2B brand with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Viavi Solutions
wiki.text: Viavi Solutions Inc., formerly part of JDS Uniphase Corporation (JDSU), is an American network test, measurement and assurance technology company based in Chandler, Arizona. The company manufactures testing and monitoring equipment for networks. It also develops optical technology used for a range of applications including material quality control, currency anti-counterfeiting and 3D motion sensing, including Microsoft's Kinect video game controller.

about: Diodes Incorporated designs and supplies discrete, analog and mixed-signal semiconductors, including power management, protection and timing chips for automotive, industrial, computing, communications and consumer markets. Revenue near 1.3 billion dollars, with factories in Asia and the US. Headquartered in Plano, Texas; founded 1959. Listed on Nasdaq (DIOD). B2B component supplier with essentially no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Diode
wiki.text: A diode is a two-terminal electronic component that conducts electric current primarily in one direction. It has low resistance in one direction and high resistance in the other.

about: Texas Instruments is a leading analog and embedded processing semiconductor company, selling tens of thousands of chips and calculators (TI-84) to industrial, automotive, personal electronics and communications customers. Revenue near 16 billion dollars, with US wafer fabs in Texas, Utah and elsewhere. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas; founded 1930 as Geophysical Service. Listed on Nasdaq (TXN). B2B brand known to engineers and students, limited general consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Texas Instruments
wiki.text: Texas Instruments Incorporated (TI) is an American multinational semiconductor company headquartered in Dallas, Texas, United States. It is one of the top 10 semiconductor companies worldwide based on sales volume. The company's focus is on developing analog chips and embedded processors, which account for more than 80% of its revenue. TI also produces digital light processing (DLP) technology and education technology products including calculators, microcontrollers, and multi-core processors.

about: AMETEK is a US manufacturer of electronic instruments and electromechanical devices, producing precision instrumentation, sensors, motors and aerospace components for aerospace, medical, industrial and power markets. Revenue near 7 billion dollars. Headquartered in Berwyn, Pennsylvania; founded 1930. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (AME). B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Ametek
wiki.text: AMETEK, Inc. is an American multinational conglomerate and global designer and manufacturer of electronic instruments and electromechanical devices with headquarters in the United States and over 150 sites worldwide.

about: GlobalFoundries is a contract chipmaker producing semiconductors for automotive, IoT, aerospace and mobile, concentrating on specialty and mature nodes rather than leading-edge. Fabs in New York, Vermont, Germany, Singapore. Customers include AMD (original), Qualcomm and NXP, with revenue near 6.8 billion dollars. Headquartered in Malta (Saratoga County), New York; created 2009 from AMD. Listed on Nasdaq (GFS), majority owned by Mubadala. B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: GlobalFoundries
wiki.text: GlobalFoundries Inc. is a multinational semiconductor technology development, design and contract manufacturing company domiciled in the Cayman Islands and headquartered in Malta, New York. Created by the divestiture of the manufacturing arm of AMD in March 2009, the company was privately owned by Mubadala Investment Company, a sovereign wealth fund of the United Arab Emirates, until an initial public offering (IPO) in October 2021. Mubadala remains the majority owner of the company with an 82% stake.

about: Hubbell is a US maker of electrical and utility products, including grid infrastructure components, wiring devices, connectors and lighting for utilities, industrial, telecom and commercial customers. Revenue near 5.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Shelton, Connecticut, founded 1888. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (HUBB). B2B brand, with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Hubbell Incorporated
wiki.text: Hubbell Incorporated, headquartered in Shelton, Connecticut, is an American company that designs, manufactures, and sells electrical and electronic products for non-residential and residential construction, industrial, and utility applications. Hubbell was founded by Harvey Hubbell as a proprietorship in 1888, and was incorporated in Connecticut in 1905.

about: Jabil is a US electronics manufacturing services provider building products for others, including hardware for cloud and AI data centers, healthcare devices, automotive, communications and Apple components. Revenue near 29 billion dollars and around 140,000 employees in over 30 countries. Headquartered in St Petersburg, Florida; founded 1966. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (JBL). B2B manufacturer with no consumer brand profile.

wiki.title: Jabil
wiki.text: Jabil Inc. is an American multinational manufacturing company involved in the design, engineering, and manufacturing of electronic circuit board assemblies and systems, along with supply chain services, primarily serving original equipment manufacturers. It is headquartered in the Gateway area of St. Petersburg, Florida. It is one of the largest companies in the Tampa Bay area.

about: Rapidus is a Japanese semiconductor foundry company founded in 2022 by Toyota, Sony, NTT, SoftBank, Denso, NEC, Kioxia and MUFG, aiming to produce 2-nanometer logic chips in Chitose, Hokkaido by 2027 with technology help from IBM. Backed heavily by Japanese government subsidies. Headquartered in Tokyo. Funding shown is around 726 billion yen. Pre-revenue B2B manufacturer with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Rapidus
wiki.text: Rapidus Corporation is a semiconductor manufacturer headquartered in Chiyoda, Tokyo, Japan. Rapidus was established in August 2022 with the support of eight major Japanese companies: Denso, Kioxia, MUFG Bank, NEC, NTT, SoftBank, Sony, and Toyota. The goal of Rapidus is to increase advanced semiconductor manufacturing capacity with a 2 nm process by 2027.

about: Solstice Advanced Materials is a US specialty materials company spun out of Honeywell in October 2025, making refrigerants (Solstice low-global-warming products), electronic materials, nuclear and medical packaging materials and fluorine chemicals. Customers are industrial and electronics manufacturers. Headquartered in Morris Plains, New Jersey. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (SOLS). B2B brand, little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Solstice Advanced Materials
wiki.text: Solstice Advanced Materials, Inc. is an American specialty materials company, based in Morris Plains, New Jersey, that was formed on October 30, 2025, as a spin-off of Honeywell's specialty materials business. The company listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol SOLS and initially as a component of the S&P 500 index.

about: TeamSystem is Italy's largest provider of management software, offering cloud accounting, payroll, e-invoicing and ERP software to small and mid-size businesses and accountants in Italy, Spain, Germany and France. Headquartered in Pesaro, Italy; founded 1979. Owned by private equity firm Hellman & Friedman (majority investment from 2022). B2B brand with reasonable awareness among Italian accountants.

Micron Technology is a Boise, Idaho semiconductor maker, one of the three largest producers of DRAM memory and a major NAND flash maker. It sells memory and storage chips to data centers, AI server makers, smartphone, PC, automotive and industrial customers, and sells consumer SSDs and memory under the Crucial brand. Revenue is $25bn+ with around 48,000 employees and fabs in the US, Japan, Taiwan, Singapore and elsewhere. Listed on the Nasdaq (MU). Mostly a B2B brand, with Crucial giving some consumer and gamer awareness.

wiki.title: Micron Technology
wiki.text: Micron Technology, Inc. is an American multinational semiconductor company that manufactures computer memory and computer data storage products, including dynamic random-access memory (DRAM), flash memory, High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), and solid-state drives (SSDs). Founded in 1978 in Boise, Idaho, Micron is the only major American computer memory manufacturer. It is one of the "Big Three" computer memory manufacturers, along with the South Korean companies Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.

about: Command Alkon is a Hilliard, Ohio software company serving the heavy building materials industry, supplying dispatch, ticketing, ordering and logistics software for ready-mixed concrete, aggregates and asphalt producers worldwide. Its customers are material producers and contractors, paid through software subscriptions and licences. Majority-owned by private equity firm Thoma Bravo, which acquired it in 2021 (originally from Francisco Partners). Private. B2B software with no consumer visibility.

indie Semiconductor is an Aliso Viejo, California fabless chip company focused on automotive electronics, selling chips and modules for advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), LiDAR, radar, in-cabin sensing, connectivity and electrification. Customers are automakers and Tier-1 suppliers such as Aptiv, Bosch and Continental. It listed on the Nasdaq (INDI) via a 2021 SPAC merger and has acquired companies including Symeo and GEO Semiconductor. B2B component supplier, with no consumer profile.

Innoviz Technologies is an Israeli automotive LiDAR maker, with US operations noted in Santa Clara, California, whose InnovizOne and InnovizTwo sensors and perception software help vehicles see the road for autonomous driving and ADAS. Customers include automakers like BMW, Volkswagen group firm CARIAD, Mobileye (a distribution partner) and Mobileye-linked partners. Listed on Nasdaq (INVZ) after a 2021 SPAC merger with Collective Growth. B2B automotive technology supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Amkor Technology is one of the largest outsourced semiconductor packaging and test providers, headquartered in Tempe, Arizona. It assembles and tests chips for fabless firms and chipmakers such as Apple, Qualcomm and Nvidia, with plants in South Korea, Taiwan, Japan, China, Vietnam, Malaysia and Portugal, plus an Arizona advanced packaging site under construction. Revenue is about $6-7bn. Listed on Nasdaq (AMKR), with the founding Kim family a major shareholder. B2B manufacturing, no consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Amkor Technology
wiki.text: Amkor Technology, Inc. is an American semiconductor product packaging and test services provider. The company has been headquartered in Arizona since 2005, when it was moved from West Chester, Pennsylvania, also in the United States. The company's Arizona headquarters was originally in Chandler, then later moved to Tempe. The company was founded in 1968 and, as of 2022, has approximately 31,000 employees worldwide and a reported $7.1 billion in sales.

about: Applied Optoelectronics is a Sugar Land, Texas maker of optical communications chips, lasers and transceivers for data centers, cable TV broadband, telecom and FTTH networks. Customers include hyperscale cloud operators such as Amazon and Microsoft, and cable companies, with manufacturing in Texas, Taiwan and China. Listed on Nasdaq (AAOI), founded in 1997. Revenue is a few hundred million dollars a year. B2B components supplier, no consumer awareness.

Fortive is a Everett, Washington industrial technology company, spun out of Danaher in 2016, whose operating units include Fluke (test equipment), Tektronix, Gordian, Accruent and Provation, Ralliant spun off in 2025. Customers are engineers, contractors, utilities and healthcare firms worldwide, with revenue near $4bn. Listed on the NYSE (FTV). Largely B2B, though Fluke is well known to technicians; no consumer brand beyond that.

wiki.title: Fortive
wiki.text: Fortive Corporation is an American industrial technology conglomerate company headquartered in Everett, Washington. The company specializes in providing essential technologies for connected workflow solutions; designing, developing, manufacturing and distributing professional and engineered products, software and services. Their products and services are split into three strategic segments; Intelligent Operating Solutions, Precision Technologies, and Advanced Healthcare Solutions. As of December 2022, Fortive has over 18,000 employees in 60 countries worldwide.

about: Forward Industries is a design, sourcing and manufacturing company for carry cases and protective solutions, historically for medical devices (diabetic kits), tools and consumer electronics, under its Forward Industries Design Group. In 2025 it pivoted to a Solana digital asset treasury strategy, with a large private placement led by Galaxy Digital, Jump Crypto and Multicoin. Listed on Nasdaq (FORD), with the HQ shown as Austin, Texas. Small B2B supplier turned crypto treasury vehicle, with no consumer awareness.

PsiQuantum is a Palo Alto, California quantum computing company building a fault-tolerant, utility-scale photonic quantum computer with silicon photonics chips manufactured with GlobalFoundries. It is constructing sites in Brisbane, Australia and Chicago, backed by government funding. It raised $1bn in 2025 at a valuation of $7bn from BlackRock, Temasek and Baillie Gifford, with total funding above $2.5bn. Private. Prominent in deep-tech, with no consumer products.

wiki.title: PsiQuantum
wiki.text: PsiQuantum, Corp. is an American quantum computing company based in Palo Alto, California. It is developing utility-scale, fault tolerant quantum computers using silicon photonics. The company has secured government partnerships to build their first systems in Australia and the United States.

about: Silicon Box is a Singapore-based advanced semiconductor packaging company, founded in 2021, which builds chiplet integration and panel-level packaging for AI, high-performance computing and mobile customers. It runs a foundry in Singapore with a plant in Novara, Italy under development, backed by an EU-supported investment of EUR 3.2bn. Investors include Temasek and Sequoia. Private. B2B manufacturer, with no consumer visibility.

wiki.title: Silicon Box
wiki.what: Singaporean semiconductor packaging and assembly company
wiki.text: Silicon Box Pte Ltd is an independent advanced packaging and integration BEOL semiconductor company headquartered in Singapore.

about: SiTime is a Santa Clara, California fabless chip company making MEMS-based silicon timing devices, including oscillators and clock generators, which replace quartz crystals in data centers, AI servers, automotive, industrial and mobile products. Customers are electronics and telecom equipment makers. Listed on Nasdaq (SITM), it was founded in 2003 and was held by MegaChips before its 2019 IPO. B2B component supplier, no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: SiTime
wiki.text: SiTime Corporation is a publicly traded fabless chipmaker based in Santa Clara, California that develops micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS), used for timing devices in electronics.

about: TTM Technologies is a Santa Ana, California manufacturer of printed circuit boards, RF components and assemblies serving aerospace and defence, data center and networking, automotive and medical customers, with plants in North America and Asia. Revenue is about $2.5bn. Listed on Nasdaq (TTMI). B2B supplier with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: TTM Technologies
wiki.text: TTM Technologies, Inc. is an American printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturer headquartered in Santa Ana, California. Founded in 1998, the company is one of the top five PCB manufacturers in the world and the largest in North America, and the largest supplier of PCBs to the U.S. military. TTM serves customers in industries including aerospace and defense, medical, industrial, automotive, computing, and networking.

about: OSRAM is the Munich-based lighting and semiconductor company, long a household name for light bulbs and automotive lighting, which became part of ams OSRAM in 2020 when Austria's ams AG acquired it for about EUR 4.6bn. It makes LEDs, lasers, sensors and automotive lamps (Osram and Sylvania brands). Customers are carmakers, electronics firms and consumers. Part of ams OSRAM (SIX: AMS). Well-known consumer lighting brand, especially in Germany.

wiki.title: Osram
wiki.text: OSRAM Licht AG is a German company that makes electric lights, headquartered in Munich and Premstätten (Austria). OSRAM positions itself as a high-tech photonics company that is increasingly focusing on sensor technology, visualization and treatment by light. The company serves customers in the consumer, automotive, healthcare and industrial technology sectors. The operating company of OSRAM is OSRAM GmbH.

about: Repay (REPAY Holdings) is an Atlanta, Georgia electronic payment processing company providing integrated card and ACH processing, merchant acquiring and bill-pay software to businesses in niche verticals such as auto lending, consumer finance and healthcare. Revenue is near $300m. Listed on Nasdaq (RPAY) since a 2019 SPAC combination with Thunder Bridge. B2B fintech, with no consumer brand awareness. Crunchbase lists the country as Georgia (the US state).

KnowBe4 is a Clearwater, Florida security awareness training and simulated phishing platform used by over 70,000 organisations to train employees. Vista Equity Partners took it private in 2023 for about $4.6bn, and it later acquired Egress and was folded into the KnowBe4 and Egress offering. Revenue was near $350m before the buyout. Private. B2B cybersecurity brand with high awareness among IT teams but little consumer awareness.

Legrand is a French maker of electrical and digital building infrastructure, based near Limoges and managed from Croissy-Beaubourg, producing switches, sockets, cable management, data center power and connected home products under brands such as Legrand, Bticino and Arnould. Revenue is about EUR 8.5bn with over 38,000 employees, selling in nearly 90 countries. Listed on Euronext Paris (LR). B2B and installer-focused, but switches and sockets are in most European homes; modest consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Legrand (company)
wiki.text: Legrand S.A. is a French industrial group historically based in Limoges in the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region.

about: Progress Software is a Burlington, Massachusetts enterprise software company selling application development, data integration, content management and cybersecurity tools, such as Telerik, Sitefinity, MarkLogic, MOVEit and ShareFile, to developers and businesses. Revenue is around $950m. Listed on Nasdaq (PRGS). B2B software with recognition among developers, and little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Progress
wiki.text: Progress is movement towards a perceived refined, improved, or otherwise desired state. It is central to the philosophy of progressivism, which interprets progress as the increasing positive liberty of society; it views it as primarily achievable through direct societal action, as in social enterprise or through activism, but being also through natural sociocultural evolution – that progressivism holds all human societies should strive towards.

about: Alliance Laundry Systems is a Ripon, Wisconsin manufacturer of commercial laundry equipment, selling washers and dryers under the Speed Queen, UniMac, Huebsch, IPSO and Primus brands. Customers are laundromats, multi-housing laundry operators, hotels, and institutions, plus Speed Queen home laundry sold to consumers. Revenue runs in the billions of dollars with global distribution. Long owned by private equity (BDT Capital and others); it completed a US IPO in 2025 (NYSE: ALH). Speed Queen has solid consumer recognition in North America; mostly B2B overall.

wiki.title: Alliance Laundry Systems
wiki.text: Alliance Laundry Systems LLC is an American provider of commercial laundry systems. The company designs, manufactures, and markets a line of commercial and industrial laundry equipment under various brands in over 100 countries. Among the company's products are washers, drying tumblers and ironers for the coin laundry, multi-housing laundries, institutional laundries and laundries for consumer residences. Alliance Laundry Systems manufactures products under the brands Speed Queen, Primus, Huebsch, IPSO, and UniMac. The company was founded in 1998 and is based in Ripon, Wisconsin. However, Alliance claims Speed Queen's founding date of 1908 as

about: GoPro is a San Mateo, California maker of action cameras (HERO series, MAX 360), mounts and accessories, plus a subscription service for cloud storage and editing. Founded in 2002 by Nick Woodman, it sells through retailers and online to consumers, adventure athletes and creators in about 100 countries. Listed on Nasdaq (GPRO) since 2014; revenue has fallen from a peak above $1.5 billion. Strong consumer brand in action sports and has a history of sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: GoPro
wiki.text: GoPro, Inc. is an American technology company founded in 2002 by Nick Woodman that went public in 2014 on the Nasdaq stock exchange under the ticker GPRO. It manufactures action cameras and develops its own mobile apps and video-editing software. GoPro cameras are widely used for adventure sports, travel recording, and outdoor activities. Founded as Woodman Labs, Inc, the company is based in San Mateo, California.

about: Advanced Energy Industries is a Denver, Colorado-based maker of precision power conversion and control systems (Fort Collins origins) for semiconductor equipment, industrial thin-film, data center, telecom and medical applications. Founded in 1981, listed on Nasdaq (AEIS), with roughly $1.5 billion annual revenue. Customers are equipment manufacturers such as Applied Materials and Lam Research. B2B, no consumer brand awareness.

ContourGlobal is a London-headquartered power generation company, founded in 2005, that owns and operates thermal, hydro, wind and solar plants across Europe, Latin America, Africa and the US. It sells electricity mainly under long-term contracts to utilities and grids, and has been growing its clean energy share. KKR acquired it in 2022 and took it private from the London stock market. B2B energy, with little consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: ContourGlobal provides a growth platform that focuses...

wiki.title: ContourGlobal
wiki.text: ContourGlobal Limited is a British power generation business. It was listed on the London Stock Exchange until it was acquired by KKR in December 2022.

about: Semtech is a Camarillo, California supplier of analog and mixed-signal semiconductors, including LoRa wireless chips for IoT, signal integrity products for data centers, and protection devices, sold to electronics makers in data center, industrial and consumer markets. Founded in 1960, listed on Nasdaq (SMTC), with annual revenue around $900 million. Customers are OEMs, not end consumers. B2B component supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Semtech
wiki.text: Semtech Corporation is an American supplier of analog and mixed-signal semiconductors and advanced algorithms for consumer, enterprise computing, communications and industrial end-markets. It is based in Camarillo, Ventura County, Southern California. It was founded in 1960 in Newbury Park, California. It has 32 locations in 15 countries in North America, Europe, and Asia.

about: NextNav is a McLean, Virginia-based company that operates a terrestrial positioning network providing 3D location, including floor-level altitude, and resilient GPS-alternative timing and navigation using licensed spectrum. Customers are wireless carriers, government and public safety agencies. Listed on Nasdaq (NN) since 2021, with reported funding of about $913 million. B2B technology with very limited consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: NextNav
wiki.text: NextNav, Inc. is the developer of a 3D geolocation service known as Metropolitan Beacon System (MBS), a wide-area location and timing technology designed to provide services in areas where GPS or other satellite location signals cannot be reliably received. MBS consumes significantly less power than GPS and includes high-precision altitude. In the United States, NextNav operates its MBS network over its spectrum licenses in the 920-928 MHz band. The company went public on Nasdaq in October 2021 with a merger with special-purpose acquisition company Spartacus Acquisition Corporation.

about: Mirion Technologies is an Atlanta, Georgia-based provider of radiation detection, measurement, analysis and monitoring products for nuclear power plants, defense, healthcare (radiation therapy QA) and laboratories. Listed on NYSE (MIR) after a 2021 SPAC merger with GS Acquisition Holdings II, with annual revenue near $900 million. Customers are utilities, hospitals, governments and labs. B2B, no consumer brand awareness.

EnPro Industries is a Charlotte, North Carolina-based industrial technology company, listed on NYSE (NPO), making sealing products, engineered materials and specialty components for semiconductors, life sciences, aerospace and general industry (Garlock, Stemco, Technetics). Revenue is about $1 billion. Customers are industrial and semiconductor manufacturers. B2B, with no consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Enpro Industries
wiki.text: Enpro is a US-based industrial technology company that designs and manufactures products and materials for technology-intensive sectors. The company serves industries such as semiconductors, aerospace, power generation, heavy-duty trucking, agricultural machinery, chemical processing, pulp and paper, and life sciences from 61 primary manufacturing facilities located in 12 countries, worldwide. It is organized under three segments: Sealing Technologies, Advanced Surface Technologies, and Engineered Materials.

about: Park Place Technologies is a Cleveland, Ohio IT infrastructure services company that provides third-party maintenance, hardware support, network monitoring and data centre services for servers, storage and networking equipment from vendors such as Dell, HPE and Cisco. It serves thousands of enterprise customers in more than 150 countries and has grown through acquisitions. Founded 1991; privately held with private equity ownership. Revenue comes from maintenance contracts. B2B IT services brand with little consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Park Place Technologies is an IT company that provided...

about: Frore Systems is a San Jose semiconductor company that makes AirJet solid-state active cooling chips, a silent, thin cooling technology for laptops, tablets, phones and data centres that replaces fans. Founded 2018 by Seshu Madhavapeddy, it has raised funding from venture investors including Mayfield at a valuation reported near 1 billion dollars. Customers are device makers. Revenue is chip sales. B2B component brand with limited consumer visibility, though recognised in tech media.

Craftsman Automation is an Indian engineering company based in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu and listed on the NSE and BSE, making high-precision powertrain and aluminium components such as engine blocks, cylinder heads and crankcases for commercial vehicles, tractors and cars, plus industrial and storage solutions. Customers include Ashok Leyland, Daimler, Cummins and Tata Motors. Revenue is above 50 billion rupees. Founded 1986. B2B manufacturer with minimal consumer awareness.

WT Microelectronics is a Taiwanese electronic components distributor headquartered in Taipei and listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (3036), distributing semiconductors, memory and other chips for brands such as Samsung, Qualcomm, Analog Devices and others to electronics manufacturers across Asia. Revenue is in the hundreds of billions of Taiwan dollars. B2B distributor with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: WT Microelectronics Co., Ltd. provider focusing on the globa...

about: Relativity is a US legal technology company based in Chicago that provides RelativityOne, a cloud platform for e-discovery, investigations and compliance that uses AI to review documents in litigation, with users including law firms, corporations and governments. Founded 2001 as kCura, it is controlled by Silver Lake and has more than 300,000 users worldwide. Revenue comes from software subscriptions. B2B legal technology brand, known in the legal industry.

SiFive is a US semiconductor company headquartered in Santa Clara, California that designs and licenses processor IP based on the open RISC-V instruction set, selling core designs and development platforms to chipmakers and system companies for data centres, automotive, and embedded applications. Founded 2015 by the inventors of RISC-V at UC Berkeley, it has raised funds from Sutter Hill, SK Hynix, Intel Capital and Qualcomm Ventures. Customers are semiconductor firms. B2B technology brand with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: SiFive
wiki.what: Fabless semiconductor company providing RISC-V processors
wiki.text: SiFive, Inc. is an American fabless semiconductor IP company and provider of commercial RISC-V processors and silicon chips based on the RISC-V instruction set architecture (ISA). Its products include cores, SoCs, IPs, and development boards.

about: MatX designs custom AI semiconductors, chips built to run large language models efficiently for training and inference. Founded in 2022 by former Google TPU engineers Reiner Pope and Mike Gunter, based in Mountain View, California. Customers are AI labs and cloud companies. Crunchbase shows about $625 million in total funding, the latest in February 2026. Private. Deep B2B brand, known in the AI hardware industry, with no consumer visibility.

Nearfield Instruments develops and supplies metrology and inspection equipment for semiconductor manufacturing, using atomic force microscopy based tools to measure nanoscale structures on chips, notably its QUADRA platform. Customers are leading chipmakers and equipment partners. Spun out of TNO and TU Delft, it is based in Rotterdam, Netherlands. Crunchbase shows about $598 million in total funding, latest June 2026. Private. Deep B2B industrial brand with no consumer visibility.

Soitec produces engineered semiconductor substrates, notably silicon-on-insulator (SOI) wafers, plus silicon carbide and other materials used in chips for smartphones, cars and data centres. Customers include TSMC, GlobalFoundries and Samsung. Headquartered in Bernin near Grenoble, France, and founded in 1992 as a spin-out of CEA-Leti. Annual revenue is around 1 billion euros. Listed on Euronext Paris (SOI). Crunchbase shows $500 million in funding. Deep B2B brand with no consumer visibility.

wiki.title: Soitec
wiki.text: Soitec is a French multinational corporation that manufactures substrates used in the manufacturing of semiconductors.

about: Synchron develops a brain-computer interface, the Stentrode, a device delivered through blood vessels that lets people with paralysis control digital devices by thought. Founded in Australia and now based in Brooklyn, New York, it runs clinical trials and has partnerships with Nvidia and Apple. Revenue would come from medical device sales, so it is currently pre-commercial. Crunchbase shows about $605 million in total funding. Private. Strong media profile in neurotechnology.

wiki.title: Beckman Coulter
wiki.text: Beckman Coulter, Inc. is an American company that develops, manufactures, and markets products relevant to biomedical testing. It has been a subsidiary of Danaher Corporation since 2011. It operates in the industries of diagnostics under the brand name Beckman Coulter and life sciences under the brand name Beckman Coulter Life Sciences. The company was established in 1935 as National Technical Laboratories, and has become an international company through growth and acquisitions of other life sciences organizations.

about: Lake Mary, Florida, public safety software provider formed in 2019 by merging Superion, TriTech, Zuercher and others, selling dispatch, records and 911 software to police, fire and emergency services. Owned by Bain Capital. B2B government software with no consumer visibility. Sells subscriptions and implementation services, with thousands of agencies as customers. Its products include computer-aided dispatch, mobile apps, jail management and records software, and it has thousands of public safety customers.

VisionPower Semiconductor Manufacturing Company is a Singapore-based chip manufacturing joint venture in which Vanguard International Semiconductor (VIS) partnered with NXP to build a 12-inch wafer fab. Funding of about $1.6 billion shown. B2B manufacturing company with no consumer visibility. It supplies mature-node analogue and power chips to automotive and industrial customers. The plant is planned to supply chips for automotive, industrial and consumer electronics, with production starting around 2027.

IQM Quantum Computers is a Finnish company that builds superconducting quantum computers, selling full-stack systems and on-premises quantum machines to supercomputing centres, universities and research labs, along with cloud access. Spun out of Aalto University and VTT in 2018, it is based in Espoo and has operations in Munich and elsewhere. It has raised over 600 million dollars, including a 320 million dollar round in 2025 led by Ten Eleven Ventures, and is one of Europe's best-funded quantum companies. B2B deep-tech with little general consumer awareness.

Winbond Electronics is a Taiwanese semiconductor company that designs, manufactures and sells memory chips: serial flash, specialty DRAM and secure flash, used in automotive, industrial, consumer electronics and telecom products. It operates its own fabs in Taichung and Kaohsiung, Taiwan, and is listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (2344), founded in 1987 and part of the Walsin Lihwa group. Revenue is about 2 billion dollars. B2B component supplier with limited consumer visibility.

Bel Fuse is a US manufacturer of electronic components for networking, power and circuit protection: magnetic connectors, power supplies, converters, fuses, and connectors used in data centres, defence, aerospace, automotive and telecom equipment. It sells B2B to OEMs and distributors, with factories in Asia and Europe and annual revenue around 600 million dollars. Founded in 1949, it is headquartered in Jersey City, New Jersey, and listed on Nasdaq (BELFA, BELFB). Little consumer brand awareness.

Exosens is a French manufacturer of advanced electro-optical technologies, including night vision tubes, detectors, X-ray and neutron imaging and photomultipliers, supplying defence, industrial, scientific and nuclear markets. Formerly Photonis, it is headquartered in Merignac near Bordeaux, listed on Euronext Paris (EXENS) since 2024, and has revenue of about 400 million euros. Customers include defence ministries and equipment makers. B2B and little consumer brand awareness.

GrafTech International is a US manufacturer of graphite electrodes used in electric arc furnaces for steelmaking, and of petroleum needle coke. Customers are steel producers around the world, and operations include plants in the United States, Mexico, Spain and France. Headquartered in Parma (Brooklyn Heights), Ohio and listed on the NYSE (EAF), it was majority owned by Brookfield. It has struggled with falling prices and Chinese competition. B2B industrial supplier with no consumer brand awareness.
